issues.legal_issue: An independent administrator should be appointed to preserve and manage disputed property pending resolution of the suit where there is a prima facie claim to the property and a risk that it will be dissipated.
material_facts: The suit concerned whether the disputed properties were individually owned or belonged to a Hindu Undivided Family, and the court found a prima facie case that they belonged to the family.
The person controlling the properties had reported them as Hindu Undivided Family property in tax returns for several years, although he later said this was done on legal advice to save tax.
An injunction barred that person from dealing with scheduled suit properties.
He had sold more than six thousand company shares, including more than two thousand shares listed as suit property.

The appeal challenged the refusal to appoint a Receiver, and the court considered independent management necessary to preserve the suit properties and avoid further allegations of breach of the injunction.
issues.conclusion: The refusal to appoint a Receiver was set aside, and an Administrator was appointed to take charge of the scheduled suit properties, manage and preserve them, and exercise the powers and duties of a Receiver except as otherwise directed.
issues.legal_principle: Where a prima facie case exists and the circumstances make it just and convenient to place disputed property under independent control to prevent its dissipation and preserve it pending suit, the court may appoint an Administrator with the powers and duties of a Receiver. The judgment cites no statutory provisions or earlier cases for this decision.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_appoint_receiver: A party appealed an order refusing to appoint a Receiver over property in dispute in a pending suit.
predicates.prima_facie_claim_to_disputed_property: The court found a prima facie basis for the claim that the disputed property belonged to a family estate rather than to the person controlling it individually.
predicates.sale_of_suit_property: The person controlling the disputed property sold assets that were included among the suit properties.
predicates.risk_of_dissipation_under_existing_injun: An injunction restricted dealings with the suit property, but the circumstances indicated a risk that the property could nevertheless be dissipated or disposed of.
predicates.independent_administrator_appointed_to_p: The disputed property is placed under an independent Administrator's control for management and preservation pending resolution of the suit.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges refusal to appoint a Receiver, a prima facie claim to disputed property together with a sale of suit property or a risk of dissipation despite an existing injunction supports placing the property under an independent Administrator's control for preservation.
